questions: What target GPU utilization should trigger scale-up?
How many pre-warm/burst nodes are reasonable for 3x traffic spikes?
Impact on cost for different burst pool sizes?
transcript:
[00:00] Alex (AE): Hey everyone thanks for joining, this is our 12/14 weekly POC sync with Nexify — quick roll call.
[00:07] Maya (Customer Eng): Hey Alex, hi Samir, Liz.
[00:10] Jordan (Product): Morning all, joining from product.
[00:13] Samir (SE): Samir here, I'll go over the sizing notes we sent.
[00:18] Alex: Cool. Quick agenda — 1) review last week's soak, 2) autoscale tuning, 3) burst planning and next steps. Anything to add?
[00:25] Maya: Sounds good, also we have a couple security questions later.
[00:28] Priya (Security): Yes a few KMS flow clarifications.
[00:31] Alex: Great. Samir, you want to kick off with the soak results?
[00:35] Samir: Yeah, quick summary. Last 48 hours we saw the pilot avg RPS ~ 42, peak sustained 180 for ~6 minutes during spikes. p50 latency for completion was ~250ms, p95 ~780ms, p99 hit 1.8s when we had cold starts. Note on batching: we were using a 32-token avg payload for the batcher which gave better throughput but increased p95 a bit.
[01:03] Maya: That's consistent with what we saw. The one user flow that hits the summarization pipeline is heavier — avg token lengths closer to 220 tokens in that route.
[01:12] Jordan: Right, that heavy route was only ~8% of calls but accounts for ~28% of GPU time.
[01:19] Samir: Exactly. For Dedicated sizing we had previously recommended a baseline of 6x A100 nodes with a 2-node burst pool for transient spikes. With the traffic you described we think that's undersized for the 3x burst scenarios — need either larger burst pool or pre-warmed nodes.
[01:36] Ethan (Infra): Quick q — are those A100s or H100s in the estimate? Cost wise H100 is higher but latency improves for long contexts.
[01:44] Samir: The initial estimate assumed A100 80GB. If you want H100 we can provide delta; H100 cuts the p95 by roughly 25% for your long-context route but increases monthly committed cost.
[01:56] Alex: Let's talk autoscaling config. We propose target_gpu_util = 60% for scale-up, cooldown 180s, scale step +2 nodes up to burst pool size, and a scale-down target_gpu_util = 30% with longer cooldown 600s so we don't thrash. Thoughts?
[02:16] Maya: 60% sounds reasonable, our infra team worried about cold-starts causing p99 spikes during scale-up.
[02:23] Samir: That's why we suggest a small pre-warm pool of 2 nodes always on, and a burst pool of 4 that can come up quickly. We also have warm-standby images which shave boot by ~30-40s.
[02:36] Jordan: How quick is "come up quickly"? If the burst pool takes 2m to land, that's still painful.
[02:41] Samir: With pre-warm + warm-standby you get functional readiness ~40-60s depending on image pull; full model load can be another 20-30s but KV cache is empty until warmed. So expect initial p99 degradation for the first minute unless you pre-warm model cache or use cached prefix KV.
[03:01] Maya: We can try model pre-warm for the heavy route — run a synthetic hit to populate the KV. We'll add that to the soak.
[03:07] Priya: On the KMS point — for Private we need to validate envelope encryption and whether key rotation is supported without downtime. Also audit logs retention for 13 months.
[03:18] Liz (Solutions Eng): We have an integration pattern for KMS with seamless rotation; rotation doesn't require downtime, we rotate keys and re-encrypt new data while old keys are retained for read. We'll share the security doc.
[03:29] Alex: Good. Back to sizing — Samir, can you talk cost tradeoffs if they go H100 vs A100 and expand burst pool from 2 to 4?
[03:37] Samir: Sure. Rough numbers: baseline 6x A100 committed = $Xk/mo (placeholder), adding burst pool of 4 A100 on demand increases cost only during bursts but you'd see ~20-30% cost delta in our estimate if those bursts occur frequently. H100 baseline instead would increase committed price by ~45% but reduce per-token latency and might reduce the needed cluster size by 1-2 nodes because of increased throughput per GPU. We'll put concrete numbers in the spreadsheet.
[04:05] Jordan: Important for us is predictability. If committed dedicated capacity with smaller burst pool gives predictable p95 we might prefer that.
[04:13] Maya: Also can Redwood Dedicated do scheduled scale rules? e.g., bump capacity for 9am\u201311am on weekdays when we see traffic?
[04:21] Samir: Yes scheduled policies are supported, you can combine schedule + utilization-based autoscale + manual override. That helps with predictable morning spikes.
[04:29] Ethan: Can the autoscaler consider queue length as a signal? We saw queueing lead to head-of-line latency during the big spike.
[04:36] Samir: We support custom metrics; many customers use a composite signal like max(gpu_util, avg_queue_length) and then a scoring threshold to trigger scale. We'll include a sample config.
[04:45] Maya: Nice. Regarding batch sizes — when we bumped batcher window to 200ms throughput improved but p95 suffered for the lighter requests. Any suggestions?
[04:53] Liz: Adaptive batching is helpful — set per-route max_batch_size and a tight latency cap for low-latency routes. For heavy summarization route you can allow longer batch windows. Redwood Optimize can also suggest per-route batch profiles based on real traffic.
[05:08] Jordan: Ok let's lock on immediate changes: 1) run 24h soak with synthetic bursts and model pre-warm for heavy route, 2) Redwood to send updated sizing + H100 delta by 12/16, 3) Samir to post autoscale config snippet, 4) Priya to confirm KMS requirements.
[05:23] Alex: Perfect. Anything else on risk/timeline?
[05:26] Priya: We also want to ensure audit logs ship to our Splunk — retention policy and schema.
[05:31] Liz: We support log shipping to Splunk and S3 with configurable retention; will attach schema.
[05:37] Maya: A question on SLA — if we go Dedicated with reserved capacity, what's the SLA for model availability and failover to fallback models?
[05:44] Alex: Our Dedicated SLA covers availability and we can configure fallback policies to a smaller model variant if there's a node outage; that reduces latency but keeps the app online. We'll include the SLA doc in the follow-up.
[05:55] Jordan: One more — competitor question: does Redwood provide cost analytics at token level similar to what we've seen from Anthropic?
[05:59] Alex: Yes per-token cost breakdown and token-level billing is available in Console; we'll show that in the next demo.
[06:06] Maya: Great. Any blockers to the 24h soak?
[06:09] Ethan: We'll need the synthetic hit script; can Redwood provide one?
[06:12] Samir: Yes we'll share a JMeter/K6 script and a small harness that hits the heavy route with configurable token lengths and concurrency. Link will be in the follow-up.
[06:21] Alex: OK let's recap next steps and owners.
[06:25] Samir: Action items I'll post to the shared doc and the sizing spreadsheet.
[06:29] Maya: We'll start the soak on 12/19 and aim to complete by 12/21.
[06:33] Alex: Thanks everyone, we will follow up — meeting adjourned.
[06:36] END
